title: Analyzing Antibody Responses to Glycoprotein Antigens via Electron Microscopy
author: Turner, Jackson, et al.
materials: Protein G resin sepharose 4 Fast Flow
rProtein A resin sepharose Fast Flow

steps.title: Equilibrate SEC column with PBS
steps.instruction: Equilibrate the GE S200i size‑exclusion chromatography (SEC) column with PBS buffer (optional: use TBS instead).

steps.title: Inject digest and collect fractions
steps.instruction: Inject the polyclonal Fab/Fc digestion sample onto the equilibrated SEC column and collect 500 µL fractions into a 96‑well deep‑well block, collecting the entire column volume.

steps.title: Pool Fab/Fc peak fractions
steps.instruction: Identify the largest peak corresponding to ~50 kDa proteins, combine the wells belonging to this peak, and exclude any smaller preceding/following peaks, shoulders, or contaminating peaks.

steps.title: Concentrate Fab/Fc and store
steps.instruction: Concentrate the pooled Fab/Fc fractions to approximately 500 µL. Store at 4 °C with 0.025 % sodium azide for up to one month, or at –80 °C indefinitely. Clean the SEC column with 1 mL 0.5 M NaOH between runs.

steps.title: Mix Fab/Fc with HIV Env
steps.instruction: Add 15 µg HIV Env antigen to 250–500 µg polyclonal Fab/Fc (adjust amount based on antigen‑specific Fab concentration; 10–15 µg antigen is sufficient to see an SEC peak for complex isolation at 215 nm absorbance). Use a large molar excess of Fab; the exact ratio is not critical.

steps.title: Incubate Fab‑antigen complex
steps.instruction: Incubate the Fab‑antigen mixture overnight (~16 h) at 4 °C to allow binding.

steps.title: Equilibrate SEC column with TBS
steps.instruction: Equilibrate a fresh GE S200i SEC column with TBS buffer (required because PBS reacts during staining and causes precipitation).

steps.title: Inject complex and collect fractions
steps.instruction: Inject the overnight Fab‑antigen complex onto the TBS‑equilibrated SEC column and collect 500 µL fractions into a 96‑well deep‑well block, collecting the entire column volume.

steps.title: Pool antigen‑Fab complex peak
steps.instruction: Identify the small peak corresponding to the estimated antigen/Fab mass, combine its fractions, and concentrate to 200–500 µL. Adjust the concentration to ~0.04 mg/mL for negative‑stain EM by diluting with TBS as needed.

steps.title: Pool excess Fab peak
steps.instruction: Combine the peak corresponding to excess Fab, store for later use, and add 0.025 % sodium azide to prevent microbial growth.

description: The protocol below describes: isolation of human IgG from serum using Protein G, elution from resin and digestion with papain, addition of soluble HIV Env, complex purification, and deposition onto negative stain electron microscopy grids. However, this protocol can also be used to isolate IgG from animal models such as rabbit and non-human primates (NHP), with alternatives such as Protein A or CaptureSelect IgG-Fc resin, and other antigens of interest.
